subject: Recap + who signs off on pricing & timeline for BrightWorks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@brightworks.ai>, Mike Reynolds <mike.reynolds@brightworks.ai>, procurement@brightworks.ai
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + who signs off on pricing & timeline for BrightWorks

Hi Amelia / Mike —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can move to a pricing proposal you can take to finance/procurement: 

Summary of what we heard
- Workload: in-production LLM features for customer messaging and support routing; expected steady-state text generation.
- Traffic profile: pilot expected ~20M tokens/mo for the first 3 months, scaling to ~150–200M tokens/mo over 12 months. Spiky peak days expected during campaigns.
- SLAs: low-latency requirements; willingness to consider Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput if committed.

Cost context we discussed (ballpark from today's quick model)
- Suggested committed-tier price range: $700–$900 per 1M tokens with volume bands / commit discounts (12-month commit).
- Example: at 150M tokens/mo, list ~$105k–$135k/mo; with a 12-month commitment we can firm to $750/1M as a starting point.

Asks / next steps we need from you
1) Please confirm who is the economic buyer who will approve the token commitment (name + email).
2) Confirm the finance/procurement contact who will own purchase order/contracting steps.
3) Any internal timing constraints for sign-off (target date or budget cycle)?

If Mike is the right person to sign off, we can prepare a short committed-capacity proposal (PDF + one-page finance summary) and route it to him and procurement. I attached an initial price-estimate and the token forecast worksheet we used in the call for reference.

Proposed timeline from our side
- 48h: send committed pricing proposal (attached).
- 1 week: review with finance/procurement; finalize scope and commit bands.
- 2 weeks: contract/PO and onboarding kick-off (can be accelerated if procurement approves earlier).

Happy to jump on a quick call with Mike + procurement; can you propose a 30-minute slot?

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0127
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-estimate-BW-v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); BrightWorks-token-forecast.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)

From: Amelia Torres <amelia@brightworks.ai>

Date: 2026-11-29T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + who signs off on pricing & timeline for BrightWorks

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the clear recap and the materials — useful. Quick answers: 
- Economic buyer: Mike Reynolds (CFO) — mike.reynolds@brightworks.ai. He will sign off on any multi-month financial commit.
- Procurement owner: procurement@brightworks.ai (we loop them on contract/PO logistics).
- Budget context: we have a mid-fiscal-year budget available and are targeting a decision before Dec 15 so we can include the pilot in Q1 plans. Our rough internal budget band for this initiative (pilot -> commit) is $75k–$250k for the first 6 months depending on the commit level.

We like the idea of a firm 12-month committed band if the numbers hit the lower end of your range. For the pilot we want to keep flexibility to scale. Please send the committed pricing PDF to Mike and procurement and flag the pilot vs commit options.

Can we set a 30-min call on Tuesday morning (Dec 1) for Mike + procurement + our legal to run through the commercial terms? If that works for you, send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Amelia
Amelia Torres
Head of Product, BrightWorks.ai
amelia@brightworks.ai

Nice recap — quick internal note:
- If Mike signs as the economic buyer, recommend we offer a staged commit: pilot band (20M/mo) at a slightly higher $/1M (e.g., $900) then step-down to $750 for a sustained 12-mo commit >=150M/mo. That protects their flexibility and our unit economics.
- Call out Dedicated vs Hosted: if they want capacity guarantees we should include a Dedicated pricing appendix with a separate CAPEX/commit note.
- Procurement will likely ask for 30-60 day payment terms and an initial PO; be prepared to offer standard net-30 and an option for net-45 for initial pilots.

I can draft the finance one-pager and the commit band table — will drop into the estimate PDF before you send.

—Sean
Director, Sales Operations
